concepts.def: Loss of electrons, or gain of oxygen.
Gain of electrons, or loss of oxygen.
A reaction in which oxidation and reduction happen at the same time.
The corrosion of iron, which needs both oxygen and water; salt speeds it up.
Barrier methods (painting, oiling, galvanising) and sacrificial protection using a more reactive metal.
A ranking of metals by reactivity; a more reactive metal can sacrificially protect a less reactive one.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Redox, Rusting & Iron — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Redox, Rusting & Iron brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Redox, Rusting & Iron.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

What is reduction in terms of electrons?
options: Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.
Gain of electrons (the oxidation number is reduced).
Reduction means a substance becomes physically smaller in size.
Reduction means losing oxygen and oxidation means gaining oxygen — full stop.

mcqs.q: When water boils, what is broken?
options: Intermolecular forces (hydrogen bonds) between water molecules are broken — the O-H covalent bonds stay intact.
Transition metals are coloured because their nuclei emit photons in the visible range.
The covalent bonds between hydrogen and oxygen atoms are broken when water boils.
Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.

mcqs.q: Why are most transition metal complex ions coloured?
options: Transition metals are coloured because their nuclei emit photons in the visible range.
Ligands split the d-orbitals into two energy levels; electrons absorb visible light to jump between them (d-d transitions), and the complementary colour is transmitted.
Transition metal ions are coloured because they have a half-full d-subshell which naturally absorbs light.
Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Reduction”?
options: Gain of electrons; decrease in oxidation state.
EMF of a half-cell vs standard hydrogen electrode at 298 K, 100 kPa, 1 mol dm⁻³.
E°_cell = E°(cathode) − E°(anode); positive E°_cell indicates a feasible reaction.
Species that accepts electrons and is itself reduced.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Standard electrode potential E°”?
options: Species that donates electrons and is itself oxidised.
Loss of electrons; increase in oxidation state.
EMF of a half-cell vs standard hydrogen electrode at 298 K, 100 kPa, 1 mol dm⁻³.
Gain of electrons; decrease in oxidation state.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Oxidising agent”?
options: Gain of electrons; decrease in oxidation state.
EMF of a half-cell vs standard hydrogen electrode at 298 K, 100 kPa, 1 mol dm⁻³.
Loss of electrons; increase in oxidation state.
Species that accepts electrons and is itself reduced.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Electrochemical cell EMF”?
options: Gain of electrons; decrease in oxidation state.
Loss of electrons; increase in oxidation state.
E°_cell = E°(cathode) − E°(anode); positive E°_cell indicates a feasible reaction.
EMF of a half-cell vs standard hydrogen electrode at 298 K, 100 kPa, 1 mol dm⁻³.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Reducing agent”?
options: Species that accepts electrons and is itself reduced.
Species that donates electrons and is itself oxidised.
Loss of electrons; increase in oxidation state.
EMF of a half-cell vs standard hydrogen electrode at 298 K, 100 kPa, 1 mol dm⁻³.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Oxidation”?
options: Loss of electrons; increase in oxidation state.
E°_cell = E°(cathode) − E°(anode); positive E°_cell indicates a feasible reaction.
